text:
devon (support): Heads-up — Acme reported a hard p99 latency regression after the int8 calibration swap (~03:10 UTC). p99 jumped from ~1.1s to ~3.6s, multiple 401 auth failures during spikes, and a weird billing surge in their org dashboard. attaching logs they sent.
ops-bot: alert: quant-toggle:prod -> profile=prod_int8_v2 triggered p99 spike threshold. p99=3.6s, p95=1.8s.
maria (sre): Which model / quant profile exactly? any rollout id?
kevin (eng-runtime): model: open-13b, quant_profile: prod_int8_v2, rollout id: canary-2026-03-16-0310. We swapped canary at 03:10. Repro curl below.
kevin (eng-runtime): ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACME_KEY" -d '{"model":"open-13b","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":20}'
# sometimes returns 200+slow, sometimes 401
```
devon (support): pasted a short snippet from their logs: `2026-03-16T03:12:08Z request_id=abc123 latency=3.54 p99=true status=200` then `2026-03-16T03:12:09Z request_id=abc124 latency=0.98 status=401 auth=invalid_token`
sophia (ml-eng): quick hypothesis: the int8 calibration changed kv-cache layout/size for some layers, causing extra memory churn & cache thrash for certain sequence lengths. that can blow up tail latency on a fraction of requests. also calibration may change operator selection causing slower kernels on certain hardware.
maria (sre): can we narrowly route Acme back to fp16 variant while we triage? want to avoid broad rollback.
kevin (eng-runtime): yes — runtime supports per-customer model_variant override. command: `rbctl route update acme --model_variant=open-13b-fp16` (will keep their pinned model version). can do a quick flip.
devon (support): please flip and ping when done. also open billing checkpoint for their account.
kevin (eng-runtime): flipping now... `rbctl route update` -> OK. rolling traffic 100% to fp16_fallback for acme.
ops-bot: rollout finished for route acme at 03:16:22 UTC.
ops-bot: metrics update: new p99=1.15s, p95=1.05s (03:20 window).
devon (support): Acme confirms latency back to normal and 401s stopped. they still saw a billing spike between 03:10-03:18.
billing-bot: observed billing anomaly: token count billed for acme org +68% between 03:10–03:20 vs baseline. created ticket BILL-5421.
sophia (ml-eng): action items from my side: 1) reproduce locally: run calibration on few seq length distributions to observe kv-cache deltas, 2) add perf checks to calibration pipeline to detect kernel regressions, 3) create smaller candidate profile that preserves kv layout for common seq lengths.
maria (sre): infra actions: add a canary guard that blocks quant-profile swaps if p99 increases >25% in first 10 minutes for any tenant. also add per-tenant temporary fallback toggle to quickly switch to fp16.
kevin (eng-runtime): implemented temporary guard config (flag: quant.canary_p99_guard=true) and a one-click rollback in console. will add an automated rollback in next deploy.
devon (support): customer-facing notes: I told Acme we rolled them back to fp16, monitoring for billing refunds, and we'll follow up with RCA + ETA for a tuned int8 profile. they appreciated the quick flip. :thumbsup: 
maria (sre): assigning owners: sophia -> ml fix & repro, kevin -> rollout/flag work + console button, devon -> customer comms + billing ticket liaison, me -> postmortem and runbook update.
sophia (ml-eng): preliminary root cause (hypothesis): calibration changed per-layer quant scales causing extra intermediate activation sizes that cross a kernel threshold leading runtime to choose a slower memory-bound kernel on some GPUs. reproducing now with targeted inputs.
maria (sre): timeline & next steps: 1) short postmortem draft by EOD; 2) perf-test addition to calibration CI by next week; 3) add canary p99 guard to prod permanently; 4) consider defaulting canary to a smaller rollout (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
devon (support): thanks everyone. closing the immediate customer escalation. will reopen thread if Acme sees anything else.
kevin (eng-runtime): noted — will also add metric alert to surface 401 spike correlation with latency so we catch auth fallout automatically.
maria (sre): nice pivot to targeted rollback, good job.
ops-bot: incident closed for alert-id: quant-canary-376543.
devon (support): closing thread.
